title: POC weekly sync - throughput optimization
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-27 | Time: 14:00-14:42 UTC | Duration: 42m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput benchmarks from last week's continuous-batching tests, tune concurrency/queueing targets, and agree next steps for a 24h stress run. We saw strong throughput gains with batching but some p99 latency spikes under peak concurrency. Agreed to try lower max concurrency, tweak batch-timeout and prefix-caching config, and run extended test with telemetry enabled.
topics: next steps: stress test and pricing note
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet + raw logs (Devon) by 2026-05-29
Customer to run pilot traffic generator config and share arrival pattern by 2026-05-30
Schedule infra sync to review VPC peering and network egress on 2026-06-02
action_items: Devon Park - upload raw perf logs and updated benchmark spreadsheet (due 2026-05-29)
Aisha Khan - share pilot arrival pattern and token distribution (due 2026-05-30)
Ben Lowe - validate VPC peering throughput and provide current egress limits (due 2026-06-01)
transcript:
[00:00] Lina Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 42 minutes, quick agenda is results review -> tuning decisions -> next steps. Um, Devon and I will go over the numbers.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Great thanks, excited to see the batch numbers, last week we saw that 2x throughput number you mentioned but worried about the p99 spikes.
[00:20] Devon Park: Yeah so quick recap, we ran continuous batching with the model pinned to rdx-small-16q, we used batch-timeout at 8ms and max-batch-size set to 64, arrival pattern was the Poisson generator you sent, roughly 120 rps sustained with bursts to 220.
[00:38] Tom Rivera: just to clarify the bursts were synthetic, our real traffic is spikey but more like 150 sustained with little bursts, not full 220 all the time.
[00:45] Devon Park: good note. So results: overall tokens/sec improved from baseline 18k to 45k - so ~2.5x - p50 latency stayed near target at 240ms, p95 around 700ms but we observed p99 hitting 2.6s in the peak windows during burst sequences.
[01:05] Priya Menon: That p99 is the one that worries our product folks, the checkout flow is sensitive to tail latency. Are those p99s correlated with queueing depth?
[01:12] Devon Park: Yes, we saw long queue lengths when concurrent request count hit above 48 - queueing then increases batch sizes but the KV cache warmup and some kernel scheduling caused occasional tail. We're suspecting a mixture of scheduling and prefix cache misses.
[01:26] Ben Lowe: We also saw a small number of GPU context switches - maybe the runtime switching between quantized kernels produced higher latency for certain sequences, could be model size, quantization profile triggers a fallback path.
[01:38] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[01:40] Lina Martinez: right, so tradeoff is we can lower max-concurrency to keep p99 below 1s, but that reduces throughput; or we can keep concurrency high and accept some tail, or work on caching/warmup which might preserve throughput and improve tail. Thoughts?
[01:56] Aisha Khan: prefer to keep throughput close to target (we need 40k tokens/sec to meet SLA for the weekend) but with hard p99 SLA of 1s for checkout. So we want to try config changes first before conceding throughput.
[02:10] Devon Park: actionable plan - tweak batch-timeout lower to 4ms so batches form a bit faster, reduce max-batch-size to 48, and implement aggressive prefix/KV cache pinning for the top N prefixes in the workload. That should reduce tail. We can also cap concurrency to 56 instead of current 80 in the test.
[02:28] Tom Rivera: How does that affect cost? If we cap concurrency but still want throughput, do we need more instances/dedicated capacity?
[02:34] Lina Martinez: good q. Cost will go up modestly if you need more reserved capacity for the same throughput. We'll model two options in the benchmark sheet: software-only tuning vs. add 1x extra GPU pool. Devon?
[02:46] Devon Park: I'll add a cost projection row. Also note that enabling prefix caching reduces per-token compute since you avoid recomputing early layers, so you might not need a full extra GPU.
[02:58] Priya Menon: what's the behavior under longer sequences? Our median token length is 120 but the p95 is 420 tokens, do batches prefer shorter sequences which would change packing?
[03:08] Devon Park: yes packing plays a role - the runtime uses sequence-length-aware kernel selection but if you have many long sequences at once you get lower throughput. We recommended moving long-tail workloads to a fallback model variant that is cheaper to run or serves longer contexts more efficiently.
[03:25] Aisha Khan: noted. Can we see an example where you route long sequences to a 'long-context' variant?
[03:30] Devon Park: yes we can demo routing rules next week, simple policy - by token length threshold route to rdx-long-16q. That variant has slightly lower throughput but better tail consistency for long sequences.
[03:40] Ben Lowe: on networking, our initial VPC peering had MTU mismatches and we saw some packet fragmentation. I want to confirm that won't cause jitter in production.
[03:48] Lina Martinez: we'll include a short network checklist in the infra sync. Also double-check TLS termination points and whether you're doing TLS at the load balancer or in the pod.
[03:58] Aisha Khan: for security we still need the SOC2 docs and SSO integration details.
[04:02] Lina Martinez: Sofia will share the SOC2 summary and SSO SAML guide right after the call.
[04:06] Sofia Reyes: I'll drop the docs in the shared drive.
[04:08] Devon Park: back to perf, we ran a microbenchmark where we pre-warmed KV cache - that reduced p99 from 2.6s to 740ms at the same concurrency. So warming matters. The question is how to keep the cache warm under production churn.
[04:22] Priya Menon: do you have heuristics for what to pin? We have ~120k unique prefixes daily, can't pin everything.
[04:28] Devon Park: pin the top 500 prefixes representing ~60% of traffic - that's often enough. We'll help run sampling to identify top prefixes.
[04:36] Tom Rivera: what about throughput elasticity, if we have an unexpected marketing surge?
[04:40] Lina Martinez: Redwood routing policies support burst capacity and fallback to hosted replicas or cheaper variants; we can set a burst policy to allow short spikes without affecting p99 by routing lower-priority requests to a cheaper pool.
[04:52] Aisha Khan: okay that's promising. For next steps, can we get a stress test plan and schedule? We want a 24h run with realistic arrival patterns.
[04:58] Devon Park: yes we'll prepare the stress test harness, will need your arrival pattern file and a target concurrency window. Proposed run: 24h starting 2026-06-03 00:00 UTC.
[05:05] Ben Lowe: we need it to align with our change freeze, 2026-06-03 works.
[05:08] Devon Park: great. Config changes to test in the 24h run: batch-timeout 4ms vs 8ms, max-batch-size 48 vs 64, concurrency cap 56 vs 80, KV pin top-500 prefixes vs baseline. We'll run each config for 6 hours in the 24h window to get steady-state and burst coverage.
[05:27] Priya Menon: and telemetry - we need flame graphs and kernel-level traces for the p99 windows.
[05:33] Devon Park: we'll enable extended telemetry and share raw traces; note that kernel-level traces may contain internal symbols, we'll sanitize before sharing.
[05:41] Lina Martinez: ok recap and owners: Devon share updated benchmark sheet + raw logs by 5/29; Sofia share SOC2 and SSO docs today; Aisha share arrival pattern by 5/30; Ben validate VPC by 6/01; schedule infra sync 6/02. We'll run the 24h test starting 6/03. Any other items?
[05:58] Aisha Khan: quick question on pricing: if we add an extra GPU pool for headroom, what's the ballpark?
[06:04] Lina Martinez: we gave a rough number in the last deck, I'll add a line item in the sheet - approximate incremental cost 18% for one extra pool for the weekend; we'll put exact numbers in the updated sheet.
[06:14] Tom Rivera: thanks, that's helpful.
[06:16] Speaker 2: (background) all good
[06:18] Devon Park: ok we'll also run a short canary after the diag changes to ensure no regressions.
[06:22] Lina Martinez: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the links and schedule.
[06:28] Aisha Khan: thanks all, appreciate it.
[06:30] Meeting ends.
